topic: Easy AI provider login/settings UX for platform-desktop-app
stack_version_constraints: Use the existing platform-desktop-app Tauri commands and renderer package versions.
Do not introduce a new OAuth library or provider SDK in this slice.

language_options.fit: Best fit for renderer settings UX and existing ProviderAccountsPanel.
Best fit for credential storage commands, already implemented; no new native command needed.

selected_language: TypeScript/React with existing Rust/Tauri command reuse
language_decision_notes: The requested change is mainly settings ergonomics. Reusing Rust commands avoids changing credential storage/security boundaries.

architecture_options.reason: Would require provider app registration, token lifecycle, keychain storage, consent/security review, and public-release planning.

architecture_options.option: Guide official console/API key setup inside existing provider panel
architecture_options.reason: Matches official docs, existing commands, and current credential storage boundary.

architecture_theory_sources: Least-privilege credential handling: only store user-provided provider API keys, never web session cookies.
architecture_practitioner_sources: Existing provider account connection implementation and readiness tests.
architecture_decision_notes: The selected architecture improves usability without expanding authentication risk or runtime dependencies.
architecture_tradeoff_notes: API key setup is less seamless than OAuth but is official and already supported.
OS keychain storage remains a future migration before public release.

folder_structure_options.reason: ProviderAccountsPanel already owns the UI boundary.

folder_structure_options.option: Keep changes in existing MonitorShell provider panel and CSS
folder_structure_options.reason: Smallest scoped change and consistent with existing renderer tests.

folder_structure_decision_notes: No new source folder was created; only specs/history artifacts were added.
folder_semantics_notes: Provider setup remains part of workspace-monitor settings, not a separate auth product.
maintainability_notes: New test tokens assert the guide/filter/model setup UI remains present.
Provider links continue to come from the existing provider registry.
code_reference_notes: Provider credential types and commands already existed.
Existing choice/button tonal hierarchy CSS variables were reused.
issue_discussion_notes: No community issue source was used because provider authentication behavior is governed by official provider docs and local implementation contracts.

post_research_questions.what_changed_the_plan: Official docs confirmed API key/console setup should remain the supported path instead of fake in-app OAuth.
post_research_questions.what_risks_remain: Local app config secret file is not a full OS keychain solution.
post_research_questions.what_validation_is_required: Renderer tests, TypeScript check, readiness, collect, and internal package build.
